event_questions.label: E1
event_questions.not_this: A theft at the insured location (the other claim type, Ziff. 23.3); a burglary or robbery away from home (outside both types); items lost, left behind or misplaced. Breaking into a vehicle is not a burglary (a vehicle is not a container), and pickpocketing or trick theft is not a robbery: both are simple thefts.
event_questions.question: Does the file state that household contents were stolen or damaged by a theft outside the insured location that was neither a burglary (the thief forcibly entered the building or a room of it, or broke open a container in it, or unlocked it with the correct keys or codes that the thief had obtained by burglary or robbery; a vehicle is not a container) or a robbery (theft under threat or use of violence against the policyholder or a member of the household, or while they could not resist because of unconsciousness, accident or death; pickpocketing and trick theft are not robbery)?

questions.label: Q1
questions.not_this: Items merely missing where no trace, witness or circumstance points to a theft (that is open, not true); items lost, misplaced or misappropriated; a theft away from the insured location (the other claim type, Ziff. 24.2, or outside both types).
questions.question: Does the file state that household contents at the insured location (the Versicherungsort of the policy) were stolen or damaged by a burglary, a robbery or a simple theft (including vandalism), even if nothing was taken?

questions.label: Q2
questions.not_this: A guest, neighbour, tradesman or cleaner, or a person who had moved out of the household before the theft; a suspicion the file raises but does not settle is open, not true. A thief the file only calls unknown or unidentified, with nothing in the file pointing to a member of the household, does not raise this question.
questions.question: Does the file state that the theft or damage was caused by a person who lived in the same household as the policyholder at the time?

questions.label: Q3
questions.not_this: Measures already carried out; the notification of the claim itself; steps only to find the thief. Steps still to be taken to get the stolen items back or to stop them being used or sold do reduce the loss and are not excluded.
questions.question: Does the file state that measures to reduce the loss are still to be taken (not yet carried out)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.not_this: Traces that exist and are left as they were, or were only photographed; the police examining the scene; traces changed by the thief or by events outside the policyholder's control.
questions.question: Does the file state that traces of the theft (for example pry marks, a broken lock, window or container) have been removed or altered, or are to be removed or altered, by the policyholder or on their behalf, for example by repair or cleaning?

questions.label: Q5
questions.not_this: A motor scooter or motorcycle; bicycle parts or accessories alone. A stated e-bike leaves the fact open: the form's word 'Fahrrad' does not decide it.
questions.question: Is a bicycle among the stolen or damaged items?

questions.label: Q6
questions.not_this: The claimant simply acted quickly or found it convenient, without a danger of further loss before the insurer could be asked.
questions.question: Does the file state that the measures could not wait for the insurer's instruction because of imminent danger (Gefahr im Verzug)?

questions.label: Q7
questions.not_this: Only some vouchers cannot be obtained (then the others are still needed); the vouchers have not been attached yet or not been looked for; finding them is merely inconvenient.
questions.question: Does the file state that the original purchase vouchers for all of the stolen or damaged items cannot be obtained, or only at considerable cost (not even as a duplicate from the seller)?

questions.label: Q8
questions.not_this: A lock change made for another reason; emergency doors, glazing or locks put in after the event; the repair of a damaged door or window.
questions.question: Does the claim include costs, caused by the theft, of changing or replacing keys, magnetic cards or locks at the location named in the policy, or at a bank safe the policyholder rents?

questions.label: Q9
questions.not_this: A theft through a door or window left open or unlocked, without force and without violence against a person: that is a simple theft. Breaking into a vehicle is not a burglary (a vehicle is not a container), and pickpocketing or trick theft is not a robbery: both are simple thefts.
questions.question: Was the theft a burglary (the thief forcibly entered the building or a room of it, or broke open a container in it, or unlocked it with the correct keys or codes that the thief had obtained by burglary or robbery; a vehicle is not a container) or a robbery (theft under threat or use of violence against the policyholder or a member of the household, or while they could not resist because of unconsciousness, accident or death; pickpocketing and trick theft are not robbery), and so not a simple theft?

routing.question: Which claim is this: theft or theft-related damage at the insured location (theft_at_home), a simple theft away from it (simple_theft_away), or anything else (other)? (Not this: A burglary or robbery away from the insured location (covered, if at all, by the basic cover during travel, Ziff. 26 lit. b) and any other peril: other. Neither type applies to them. Breaking into a vehicle is not a burglary (a vehicle is not a container), and pickpocketing or trick theft is not a robbery: a theft from a vehicle broken into, and pickpocketing or trick theft, away from the insured location are simple thefts away (simple_theft_away). Whether the policy includes the supplementary insurance for simple theft away, and whether an exclusion applies (for example a thief who lives in the policyholder's household), is decided within the claim type, not by this question.)

text:
Hello,

I got your letter dated 18 September 2026 about a claim under my household contents insurance, apparently with the date 20 July 2026. I am confused by it and want to answer it properly.

You ask whether I had to act straight away on that day because something was about to get worse and there was no time to ask you first. No, there was nothing like that. There was no danger of any kind, nothing urgent happened, and nothing I did that day needed doing in a hurry. Anything could easily have waited for your instructions, but there was nothing to wait for.

To be completely clear: nothing was stolen from my flat at Sonnenweg 95 in Chur and nothing there was damaged, not on 20 July 2026 and not on any other day. Nothing of mine has been stolen at all, anywhere. I never reported a loss to you, and I have nothing to report. Nina Steiner from the Rebhalde Cooperative, which owns the building, also knows of nothing that happened in my flat.

I would be grateful if you could close this file and send me a short confirmation that there is no claim in my name. I have been with you since 9 May 2023 without a single claim and I would like to keep it that way.

Best regards,
Hannah Shaw
